deckName: KS3 DT · J3 Lesson 4 · The Rescue (Teacher Deck)

slides.kicker: OUR LADY'S GRAMMAR SCHOOL · DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY
slides.heading: Lesson 4 · The Rescue
slides.notes:
WHERE THE CLASS IS: coming in, logging in, opening the class link. The lesson opens on the Do-Now, a short set of questions from earlier lessons that mark themselves. Take the register while it runs.

SAY: "Log in, open the class link and do the warm-up questions. When they are done, stop and look up."

DO NOT describe what comes after the warm-up. What pupils meet on screen is meant to be a surprise, so say nothing about it beyond these slides.

slides.heading: Today you meet functions
bullets: A function is a set of lines with a name. You write it once and use it as often as you like.
You will write your own functions in Python.
You are guided the whole way. Every step shows you what to do, and more help appears if a line is not right.
slides.notes: SAY these as they are written. Do not explain functions now: the lesson teaches them step by step.

slides.heading: Headphones on
bullets: Put your headphones on now.
Sound is part of this lesson.
No headphones? Every step still works with the sound off.
slides.notes: SAY: "Headphones on now, please. Sound is part of today. If you have no headphones, every step still works with the sound off."

slides.heading: On your own
bullets: Work on your own screen, on your own.
Do not talk to anyone about what you see, today or afterwards. Let everyone find it for themselves.
Stuck? Put your hand up.
slides.notes: SAY: "Today you work completely on your own. No talking, and no telling anyone what you see, today or at break. Let everybody find it for themselves. If you are stuck, put your hand up."

slides.heading: Read every screen
bullets: Read everything that appears on your screen before you type.
Try your best at every step. If a line is not right, the screen tells you what to change.
Your place is saved at every step.
slides.notes: SAY: "Read every word on your screen before you type. Try your best. If a line is not right, the screen tells you what to change. Your place is saved at every step."

slides.heading: Start now
bullets: Headphones on.
On your own, no talking.
Read everything on your screen.
Need to leave the room? Press Pause, bottom left.
slides.notes:
SAY: "Start now. Headphones on, on your own, and read everything on your screen."

THEN: circulate for the rest of the hour. Chapter 2 and chapter 4 are where pupils most often slow down. A stuck pupil should read the card again: help grows each time a line is wrong.

slides.heading: The last screens
bullets: At the end there are 5 questions. They are marked.
Then comes the How did it go? screen. Everybody does it.
Ten minutes left and not at the end yet? Press the button at the bottom to go to the 5 questions. You can go back afterwards.
slides.notes: SAY: "With about ten minutes to go, if you are not at the end yet, press the button at the bottom that takes you to the 5 questions. You can go back afterwards. Everybody finishes the How did it go? screen."

slides.heading: Before you leave
bullets: Finish the How did it go? screen. Nobody leaves until it is done.
Sign out every time. If you do not, the next person at this computer is still signed in as you.
Your place is saved.
Remember: tell nobody what you saw today.
slides.notes: SAY the sign-out line every lesson without exception. On shared C2k machines it is the single habit that matters most. Remind them to keep today a surprise for other classes.
